tagline: Advancing women's representation in UK business leadership
hero_kpi_rationale: No distinctive wow factor identified. The KPI selected reflects the organization's core objective: gender balance within FTSE 350 company boards.

kpis.name: Women on Boards
kpis.explanation: Proportion of women serving on the boards of FTSE 350 companies.
kpis.description: Women now represent approximately 40% of non-executive directors in the FTSE 350, a significant improvement since 2011.
kpis.signal: The UK has eliminated all-male boards in the FTSE 350.

kpis.name: Women Executive Directors
kpis.explanation: Proportion of women among executive directors in FTSE 100 companies.
kpis.description: Only 14% of executive directors in the FTSE 100 are women, highlighting a bottleneck at the top of organizations.
kpis.signal: Slow progress in executive representation despite board-level advances.

kpis.name: Women on Executive Committees
kpis.explanation: Proportion of women in executive committees of FTSE 100 companies.
kpis.description: Approximately one-quarter of executive committee members are women, up from previous years.
kpis.signal: Strong progression in senior leadership roles.

kpis.name: All-Male Boards
kpis.explanation: Number of boards with no women members in the FTSE 350.
kpis.description: The number of all-male boards has fallen from 152 to 0 in one decade through coordinated action.

kpis.name: Single Woman Boards
kpis.explanation: Number of boards with exactly one woman member.
kpis.description: The 'One & Done' phenomenon is declining, indicating deeper integration of diversity.
kpis.signal: Continued reduction in tokenistic diversity practices.

kpis.name: Women Leaders Growth
kpis.explanation: Increase in the number of women in senior leadership positions over 5 years.
kpis.description: FTSE 350 companies have seen a 20% increase in the number of women in leadership roles over four years.
kpis.signal: Significant progress across all management positions.

ai_positioning.summary: The organization makes no mention of AI strategy or initiatives. Its focus is entirely on gender diversity and corporate governance.
evidence: No mention of AI or associated technologies in provided documents.
Annual reports and communications focus exclusively on diversity metrics.
No reference to technological tools or automation to measure or promote diversity.
